## 28. Runtime internals

The rest of what the SDK exports: the pieces `serve` is built from (the manifest builder, keys, the outcome journal, the
link transport, the LLM wire, the MCP face, files and process control, client bundles). A system rarely uses these
directly; they are here so nothing is undocumented, and for tests and tools that need a seam.

### Reference: runtime internals

function · `import { manifestOf } from '@harness/sdk'`

A contract's manifest, hashed and checked against core's `Manifest` schema.

```ts

```

Refers to: [`Manifest`](#core-manifest).

#### `contractHash`

function · `import { contractHash } from '@harness/sdk'`

The hash an approved install binds its pairing grant to (`Hello.contractHash`): the manifest's contract parts, the same
whether worked out from the contract alone (fs's build, before anything runs) or by the running system. What only the
process adds is left out: its client assets, the events its implementation handles, whether it serves resources, and
its context, which may come from its context folder (all inside the approved bundle, whose hash fs checks).

```ts
function contractHash(manifest: Manifest): Promise<string>;
```

Refers to: [`Manifest`](#core-manifest).

#### `KeyStore`

interface · `import { KeyStore } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

A system's signing key pair, kept in its state folder.

```ts
interface KeyStore {
  /** The public key (Ed25519, SPKI DER, base64), making the pair on first use. */
  publicKey(): Promise<string>;
  /** Sign a challenge nonce. */
  sign(nonce: string): Promise<string>;
  /** The auto-pair secret the hub granted, if any, to re-pair with when the hub doesn't know this key. */
  autoPair(): Promise<AutoPairGrant | undefined>;
  /** Keep the newest grant (each welcome may rotate it), or forget it (`undefined`) once the hub refused it. */
  saveAutoPair(grant: AutoPairGrant | undefined): Promise<void>;
}
```

Refers to: [`AutoPairGrant`](#core-autopairgrant).

#### `scrubbedEnv`

function · `import { scrubbedEnv } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

#### `BASIC_ENV`

const · `import { BASIC_ENV } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The OS variables a child keeps (matched without case, as Windows names them `Path`, `SystemRoot`, ...).

```ts
const BASIC_ENV: readonly ["PATH", "SYSTEMROOT", "TEMP", "TMP", "TMPDIR"];
```

#### `SHARED_ENV`

const · `import { SHARED_ENV } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The harness variables a child inherits, by name: the SDK runtime tunables (`sdkEnv`: link timing, log level, ...),
never the parent's instance identity. An explicit list, not a `HARNESS_` prefix, so a parent's own settings and
secrets (the hub's admin password, signing and encryption keys) never reach a child.

```ts
const SHARED_ENV: readonly string[];
```

function · `import { permissionArgs } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

#### `CrashPolicy`

class · `import { CrashPolicy } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The restart rule for supervised processes, one per supervisor, keyed by instance: an asked-for stop or a clean exit
(for `on-failure`) stops; the restart code restarts at once; a crash restarts after `backoff`, doubling with each
crash in the last hour, and more than `maxPerHour` crashes in an hour gives up (the caller may roll back).

```ts
class CrashPolicy {
  constructor(options: CrashPolicyOptions);
  /** Decide what follows `exit` of the instance `key`, run under `policy`; `stopping` when the stop was asked for. */
  decide(key: string, policy: RestartPolicy, exit: Pick<ProcessExit, "code">, stopping: boolean): ExitDecision;
  /** Forget an instance's crashes (after a rollback, a new version or an uninstall). */
  forget(key: string): void;
}
```

#### `CrashPolicyOptions`

interface · `import { CrashPolicyOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `CrashPolicy` decides.

```ts
interface CrashPolicyOptions {
  /** The longest wait between restarts (`HARNESS_SUPERVISE_BACKOFF_MAX`). */
  readonly maxWait: number;
  /** The exit code that asks for an immediate restart (`RESTART_CODE` unless the supervisor sets another). */
  readonly restartCode: number;
  readonly clock?: (() => number) | undefined;
}
```

#### `ExitDecision`

type · `import { ExitDecision } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What to do after a process exits.

```ts
type ExitDecision =
| { readonly action: 'stopped' }
| { readonly action: 'restart-now' }
| { readonly action: 'restart'; readonly wait: number; readonly crashes: number }
| { readonly action: 'give-up'; readonly crashes: number };
```
